extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers, panel chairs, programme officers and research funders involved in grant review
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and reviewer rubric for evaluating research funding proposals, covering principles, reviewer selection, scored evaluation dimensions, conduct and panel procedures for funders and reviewers across European research programmes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence (Core Principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Excellence as the dominant criterion; identify the best research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat excellence as the principal filter when comparing proposals; used to identify the best projects for funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency (Core Principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency of the process and the criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make criteria, scoring modes and decision rationale accessible and clear to applicants and reviewers; document processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality (Core Principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Impartiality — equal treatment of comparable proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure comparable submissions are evaluated under the same criteria and conditions; avoid bias from applicant identity or institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness (Core Principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness of process to the call (proportional review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select review modes, number of reviewers and depth of review proportionate to the call's scale, value and risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality (Core Principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidentiality of submissions and reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect applicant data and review text; reviewers sign confidentiality/code-of-conduct agreements and avoid disclosure or use of privileged information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical considerations (Core Principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical considerations (research integrity, COI, harms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address conflicts of interest, research integrity issues and potential harms in evaluation; flag suspected misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruit appropriately expert reviewers (Quality Assurance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruit reviewers of demonstrably appropriate expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match reviewers' subject-matter and methodological expertise to proposal needs; document selection rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple independent reviewers; calibrate scoring (Quality Assurance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use multiple independent reviewers; calibrate scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign more than one independent expert per proposal and provide calibration exercises or guidance to align scoring practices across reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide written guidance and per-call rubrics (Quality Assurance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide written guidance and per-call rubrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue call-specific rubrics and written instructions to reviewers to ensure consistency and transparency in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor reviewer quality (Quality Assurance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor reviewer quality (dropout rate, response time, score distribution, narrative quality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track metrics such as reviewer responsiveness, score patterns and report quality; use these data to manage reviewer pools and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide feedback to reviewers post-decision (Quality Assurance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide feedback to reviewers post-decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share aggregated outcome information and quality feedback to reviewers to support continuous improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document COI declarations for every reviewer assignment (Process Integrity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Document COI declarations for every reviewer assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record conflict of interest statements and use them to exclude or reassign reviewers when necessary; keep COI records auditable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate scientific evaluation from administrative compliance check (Process Integrity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate scientific evaluation from administrative compliance check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure administrative eligibility/compliance is decided independently of scientific scoring to avoid conflating procedural and merit-based judgements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document the decision rationale (Process Integrity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Document the decision rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep clear records explaining why funding decisions were made, linking scores and narrative to outcomes for auditability and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide an appeals mechanism for procedural failure (Process Integrity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an appeals mechanism for procedural failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer applicants a route to appeal when process errors are alleged, with documented procedures and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit a sample of decisions ex-post (Process Integrity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Audit a sample of decisions ex-post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly review a subset of decisions to check adherence to procedures and quality of evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear roles for programme officers, panel chairs, individual reviewers (Governance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear roles for programme officers, panel chairs, individual reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define responsibilities (e.g., convening, moderating, scoring, conflict management) to avoid role confusion during review and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defined escalation procedures for disagreement (Governance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined escalation procedures for disagreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have explicit steps for resolving disagreements between reviewers or panels, including who can overrule or request re-evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of decision panels from funder management (Governance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Independence of decision panels from funder management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safeguard panels from undue managerial influence to preserve impartial scientific judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic rotation of panel members (Governance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Periodic rotation of panel members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rotate membership to limit entrenched bias and refresh expertise while maintaining continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify choice of review mode by call type (Methodology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice of review mode (remote-only / panel / hybrid) justified by call type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select remote, panel or hybrid formats based on complexity, number of proposals, need for discussion, and workload; document justification per call.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare mode of scoring in advance (Methodology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mode of scoring (numeric, ordinal, narrative-only) declared in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform reviewers and applicants early whether scores are numeric, rank-based or narrative-only, and provide scoring scales and interpretation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use bibliometrics as supportive, not decisive (Methodology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of bibliometrics as supportive but not decisive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ citation/metric data to inform context but avoid over-reliance; prioritize expert assessment of content and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter expertise (Reviewer Selection Profile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject-matter expertise at the level of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select reviewers whose topical knowledge matches the proposal's specific domain and research questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological expertise (Reviewer Selection Profile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological expertise appropriate to the design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reviewers understand the methods proposed (e.g., qualitative, quantitative, modelling) to judge feasibility and rigour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and institutional independence (Reviewer Selection Profile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographic and institutional independence from the applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid close institutional or geographic ties that might create conflicts or apparent bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record of delivering substantive reviews on time (Reviewer Selection Profile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Track record of delivering substantive reviews on time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer reviewers with a history of timely, thorough reviews; monitor reviewer performance metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on the funder's specific rubric (Reviewer Selection Profile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trained on the funder's specific rubric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide training or briefing to reviewers about call-specific criteria and scoring expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of demographic and disciplinary backgrounds (Reviewer Selection Profile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Diversity of demographic and disciplinary backgrounds across the panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble panels with varied perspectives and backgrounds to reduce bias and broaden expertise coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific quality / excellence (Common Evaluation Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific quality / excellence of the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended scored dimension; assess hypothesis/aims, clarity, coherence and potential to advance the field. Suggested numeric scoring: 1–5 or 1–6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and innovative potential (Common Evaluation Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality and innovative potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge novelty of ideas, approaches and potential to open new research avenues. Recommended numeric scoring: 1–5 or 1–6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance / expected impact (Common Evaluation Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance / expected impact in the field and (where relevant) for society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate significance to the discipline and broader societal or economic benefits. Consider both scientific and societal impact. Recommended numeric scoring: 1–5 or 1–6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness of methodology and feasibility (Common Evaluation Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Soundness of methodology and feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess experimental design, appropriateness of methods, risk mitigation and realistic timelines. Recommended numeric scoring: 1–5 or 1–6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the principal investigator(s) and team (Common Evaluation Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of the principal investigator(s) and team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider track record, complementary expertise, and ability to deliver the project. Recommended numeric scoring: 1–5 or 1–6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the host environment and resources (Common Evaluation Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of the host environment and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge institutional support, infrastructure and suitability of facilities for project success. Recommended numeric scoring: 1–5 or 1–6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of budget and timeline (Common Evaluation Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequacy of budget and timeline to the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether requested resources and schedule are realistic and well-justified. Recommended numeric scoring: 1–5 or 1–6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-science / data-management plan quality (Common Evaluation Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open-science / data-management plan quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate plans for data sharing, reproducibility, and open access. Consider compliance with funder policies. Recommended numeric scoring: 1–5 or 1–6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical, legal, and societal aspects addressed (Common Evaluation Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical, legal, and societal aspects addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that applications appropriately consider ethics, regulatory compliance and societal impacts. Recommended numeric scoring: 1–5 or 1–6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synergies and added value (Common Evaluation Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Synergies and added value (especially for international or consortium calls).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether consortium composition or collaborations create added scientific or societal value beyond individual partners. Recommended numeric scoring: 1–5 or 1–6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sign and uphold a code of conduct (Reviewer Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sign and uphold a code of conduct including confidentiality, COI, no-use, no-disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must formally agree to codes covering confidentiality, management of conflicts, and prohibition on using privileged information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide written justification for every score (Reviewer Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide written justification for every score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every numeric or ordinal score should be accompanied by clear narrative explaining the strengths and weaknesses that led to the mark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish strengths and weaknesses explicitly (Reviewer Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish strengths and weaknesses explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should separately list positive aspects and shortcomings, avoiding vague statements and enabling transparent feedback to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unsupported assertions and personal remarks (Reviewer Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid unsupported assertions and personal remarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments must be evidence-based and professional; avoid ad hominem language or speculative claims about applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag suspected research misconduct or duplicate submission (Reviewer Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag any suspected research misconduct or prior duplicate submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should report suspected ethical violations or prior publication/duplication concerns to the funder for investigation rather than include accusatory language in public text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibration discussion at start of every panel (Panel Norms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calibration discussion at the start of every panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels should run calibration sessions to align understanding of the scoring scale and interpretation before discussing proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal discussed by at least two reviewers plus one moderator (Panel Norms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal discussed by at least two reviewers + one moderator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure sufficient perspectives during panel discussion and use a moderator to manage debate and keep to scoring criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final ranking justified in a consensus report (Panel Norms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final ranking justified in a consensus report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce a consensus statement explaining how reviewers agreed the ranking and how scores and discussion informed the final order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory adjudication when reviewers diverge by >2 scale points (Panel Norms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where reviewers diverge by >2 scale points, mandatory adjudication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement a formal process to reconcile large score discrepancies, e.g., additional review, chair mediation, or panel re-discussion.
